instruction.text: Can you find the possessive pronouns in the following sentences?

atoms.b: 2. He wasn’t sure if the last pudding was ((yours)), so he didn’t take it.
3. The shampoo in the bathroom was ((his)), right?
4. The jeans I am wearing are ((hers)).
5. That way of cooking is very different from ((ours)).
6. Be more gentle with the vase: it’s ((theirs)).

instruction.text: Look at the example sentences and match them to the word class.

hint.text:
A possessive determiner is always followed by a noun - it is used to determine who owns something.

A possessive pronoun replaces a noun belonging to someone or something.

atoms.a: The headphones on the table are yours.

instruction.text: Look at the sentences. Do they include a possessive determiner or possessive pronoun? Match the sentences to the word category.

atoms.b: Our house has been with us for generations.
This house has been ours for generations.
